clue.text: Try to chase car with men on spree

indicators.note: out on a spree means running wild, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone tries to chase a car full of men out on a wild night.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a risk in attempting something is an idiom meaning to have a go at it.

clue.text: Scene of pastoral decay in Gibbon's work read aloud

explanation.surface: A ruined country scene appears in the historian Gibbon's writing, recited aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibbon wrote of decline and fall, but said aloud 'Gibbon's' sounds like 'Gibbons'', and Stella Gibbons wrote this comic novel of a decaying Sussex farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel is set on a run-down, gloomy farm, an emblem of rustic squalor and decline.

clue.text: Current purge is bitter

parts.note: AC is alternating current
to purge is to rid

explanation.surface: An electrical purge leaves a bitter taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an acrid smell or taste is sharp and bitter.

clue.text: Creature adding colour in clean home, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lizard brightens up a spotless house.
explanation.definitionFit: This lizard is famous for changing its skin colour to match its surroundings.

clue.text: Bowling outstanding — not before time!

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
an outstanding debt is due

explanation.surface: A cricketer's bowling stint is finally finished, and about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Late or delayed, coming only after the expected moment.

clue.text: Result of one item in programme

explanation.surface: The outcome of a single act on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome, as in 'in the event'; also a single contest or item on a sports or entertainment schedule.

clue.text: Lacking vigour when the beach is empty

explanation.surface: Feeling listless on a deserted stretch of sand.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being in a poor or depressed state; literally the moment the tide is furthest out, leaving the shore bare.

clue.text: Mike and Marguerite wrapping mother's plant

indicators.note: the two names enclose the next piece, wrapped round it

parts.note: Mike is a short form of the name Michael
the marguerite is a type of daisy
ma's, mother's

explanation.surface: Two people, Mike and Marguerite, wrap up their mum's houseplant as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an autumn-flowering aster, a garden flower.

clue.text: Line in sticker is a smear

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a bur is a prickly seed head that sticks to clothing

explanation.surface: A line on a label turns out to be a smudge.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudged, indistinct mark is a smear.

clue.text: Mountain ridge amid bare terrain

indicators.note: amid says the letters sit in the middle of the following words

explanation.surface: A ridge stands among bleak, empty country.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp mountain crest, a geological term borrowed from French.

clue.text: Marble, for example, one that may have fallen

explanation.surface: A piece of marble that might have toppled over.
explanation.walkthrough: Marble Arch is a London landmark; fallen arches are flat feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble Arch is a famous London example; fallen arches are the collapsed curves of flat feet.

clue.text: One often on a trip, possibly keen to take pounds, shillings and pence?

definitions.text: possibly keen to take pounds, shillings and pence?

explanation.surface: A frequent traveller, perhaps eager to pocket old British money.
explanation.walkthrough: LSD stood for pounds, shillings and pence in old British currency, and is also the drug; a 'head' is an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a habitual LSD user, who goes on drug 'trips'; one keen on the drug.

clue.text: Sort of, horse, one typically hard-working

explanation.surface: A kind of horse, the type that toils hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Sort of' is a print slip; read 'Sort of horse' (the wooden horse of Troy). To 'work like a Trojan' is to work very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden horse of Troy, and a byword for a tireless, diligent worker.

clue.text: Running through fence designed, say, to follow motorway turn

indicators.note: to follow puts the fence and its partner after the motorway piece
turn means the motorway's name is read backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
a pale is a fence stake, or a fence

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: designed means meant, intended

explanation.surface: A fence built to come after a bend in the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like jogging but means piercing; the M1 is the motorway linking London to the north of England, and 'say' marks a word that sounds like another.
explanation.definitionFit: Running someone through, as with a spear or sword, is piercing them, an impaling.

clue.text: Accommodation for divorced chaps at wit's end

parts.note: divorced people live apart
chaps means men

indicators.note: end takes the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Housing for divorced men who have run out of ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a type of living accommodation.

clue.text: Collection of clothing,'not top drawer stuff

explanation.surface: A pile of clothes that is not of the highest quality.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'bottom drawer' is where a bride-to-be stores linen and clothes for married life, hence not top-drawer stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for her marriage, traditionally kept in the bottom drawer.

clue.text: Having removed head, takes the skin off fish

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: to peel is to take the skin off

explanation.surface: A cook beheads and skins a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: These snake-like fish are a classic food.

clue.text: Depression ending with a drink

indicators.note: ending with places the next word at the end

parts.note: a col is a dip between mountain peaks

explanation.surface: Feeling low ends with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy soft drink flavoured with kola nut.

clue.text: Not a suitable craft for wide boys

definitions.text: Not a suitable craft for wide boys

parts.words: Not a suitable craft for wide boys
parts.note: wide boys are spivs, but read literally a slim canal vessel would not suit broad people

explanation.surface: A small boat is not for petty crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'wide boy' is British slang for a small-time crook; here it is taken literally as a broad person.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin canal boat, too slim for anyone wide.

clue.text: Sultanate presented in mostly elaborate type of language

indicators.note: presented in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: rich decoration is elaborate
Oman is a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: An Arab state shown in an ornate kind of language.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance languages descended from Latin are also called by this adjective.

clue.text: Stiff sort of personality denying right to social standing

indicators.note: denying means refusing a place to the letter

parts.note: stature means standing or status

explanation.surface: A rigid character refuses to grant rightful status.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted figure is rigid and motionless, a stiff figure.

clue.text: Spectral English lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A ghostly English lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and ghostly, like a spectre.

clue.text: Wrongly directs girl about to steer

indicators.note: about places the girl around the other piece

parts.note: a miss is a girl
to steer means to lead

explanation.surface: A young woman is about to take the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead astray, giving false guidance.

clue.text: Weep over headless bird

parts.note: to weep over something is to regret it

explanation.surface: A mourner cries over a decapitated bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron-like wading bird.

clue.text: Price of ticket for Commons

explanation.surface: The cost of a ticket to Parliament's lower house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commons is Britain's lower parliamentary house, but 'commons' also means food rations.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel charge; also food or provisions, the old sense of 'commons'.

clue.text: Siren, perhaps flashing blue one on top?

indicators.note: flashing suggests restless movement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police siren wails, perhaps with a blue light on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'blue rinse' is a bluish hair tint associated with older women, hence on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair tint is a rinse; a blue one sits on top of the head.

clue.text: Complain, getting bitter in the bar

explanation.surface: Grumbling about bitter beer in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like the English beer but belongs to the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest angrily; also a horizontal bar, as on a fence or track.

clue.text: When moving about turn to home and cry for this

definitions.text: When moving about turn to home and cry for this

indicators.note: moving about means the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Homesick travellers turn back and weep for the land of their birth.
explanation.definitionFit: One's native land, the one longed for when abroad.
